Here is the trip. It is everything you get.

Shape: city-and-culture
Leaving from: Toronto
Going to: Rome
Dates: 2027-10-09 to 2027-10-16, fixed
Travellers: 2
Ages that change the plan: 68, 71
Access needs: One of us can walk a few kilometres a day but not on cobbles for long, and stairs without a handrail are difficult.
Budget: 350 CAD, per-day
Appetite for effort: gentle
Roughest night they will accept: hotel
Would rule the trip out: Nothing that needs to be at a place before 09:00, No guided group tours

About this city-and-culture:
Pace: slow
Interests: Roman archaeology, Baroque painting, markets
In their words: We have been to Rome once, thirty years ago, and saw the obvious things then. We would rather spend a whole morning in one place than see four.

I do not know the current booking window, the visit length, or whether every room is reachable without stairs, so confirm lift access before booking.

candidates.title: Palazzo Barberini: Baroque ceilings and Caravaggio's Judith
candidates.summary: Pietro da Cortona's ceiling fresco and Caravaggio's Judith Beheading Holofernes are both here, in a palace built for the Barberini family. The building has stairs, and I do not know whether a lift serves every floor, so check that first. I could not confirm current opening days or visit length.

candidates.title: Roman Forum and Palatine Hill, unhurried
candidates.summary: The core of Roman archaeology, best taken slowly, with the Palatine offering quieter ruins above the Forum. The paths are uneven ancient stone and there are slopes and steps, so this may not suit the walker who struggles on cobbles for long; a shorter visit to the Forum alone is a possible alternative. I do not know the visit length or whether a seated rest point is available.

candidates.title: Campo de' Fiori market, morning browse
candidates.summary: A working market with fruit, flowers, cheese and cured meats, which suits a slow morning of looking and tasting. It is busiest in the late morning, and the cobbled square is uneven, so arrive well after the opening hours and sit down for coffee nearby. I do not know the exact stall hours on each day.

candidates.title: Santa Maria del Popolo: Caravaggio's Cerasi Chapel
candidates.summary: A small church with two Caravaggio altarpieces in the Cerasi Chapel, free to enter and easy to combine with a slow walk. The threshold and floor are stone, and I do not know the opening hours or whether a donation is expected.

candidates.title: Palazzo Doria Pamphilj: Velázquez and a private collection
candidates.summary: A private family palace holding Velázquez's portrait of Innocent X and a dense Baroque painting collection. Its rooms are more personal than the big museums, and I do not know whether a lift is available or how long a visit takes.

candidatesAccepted.title: Hotel in the Centro Storico, near the Campo de' Fiori market
candidatesAccepted.summary: A small hotel within walking distance of the Baroque centre and the Campo de' Fiori market, so the morning in one place can be done without a long walk back. Central Rome is mostly cobbled and some older hotels have steep stairs, so ask before booking for a room with lift access or on the ground floor and a step-free entrance. I have not checked availability or current rates for these dates, so the band is an estimate in euros and should be compared with the 350 CAD per day budget.

candidatesAccepted.title: Hotel near Termini with lift access and a quieter walk to the centre
candidatesAccepted.summary: A mid-range hotel near Termini station, close to the Esquilino market, with a shorter walk on flatter streets to the main sights than the centre offers. Lift access is not something I can confirm, so it should be checked directly with the hotel given the stairs concern. The rate band is an estimate I have not verified for October 2027, in euros, for the party as a whole.

candidatesAccepted.title: Hotel in Prati, on wide streets near the Vatican
candidatesAccepted.summary: A quieter residential district with wider pavements than the historic core, a reasonable choice for someone who needs a gentler walk, and close to the Vatican museums for a slow morning there. Lift and step-free access are unconfirmed and should be asked about. Rates and availability for these dates are unchecked; the euro band is an estimate for the room for two.
